_provenance.what: Apparent geocentric ecliptic longitude and latitude of the grahas, the mean lunar node, Greenwich apparent sidereal time, the true obliquity and the sidereal-free (tropical) ascendant at four places, on a stratified grid.
_provenance.why: The site's positions came from one library and were compared to nothing. This is a sky from a different lineage of code, so reference-verify.mjs can fail when the engine drifts.
_provenance.frame: True ecliptic and equinox of date, apparent place. Comparable to window.__kEclip(name, ms).trop with no ayanamsa on either side.
_provenance.timescale: Compare on jdTT, never on iso/jdUTC. A position is a function of TT; astronomy-engine takes its Date as UT and applies its own Delta-T, while jdTT here is TAI-derived and predicts nothing. Comparing at a common UTC therefore compares two Delta-T models as well as two skies -- at 2150 they differ by roughly 400 s, which displaces the Moon by about 219 arcsec and is indistinguishable from an engine fault until the residual is bucketed by epoch. The harness solves for the UT that puts the engine at each sample's TT, and reports the Delta-T disagreement separately as the stated uncertainty it is rather than failing on it.
_provenance.reference: ERFA (IAU SOFA) via astropy: epv00 for the Sun, moon98 for the Moon, plan94 for the five tara-grahas, gst06a and obl06/nut06a for Earth orientation.
_provenance.referenceAccuracyNote: plan94's own documented longitude error over 1000-3000 CE. The per-body bars in the harness are derived from these, which is why Jupiter's and Saturn's are loose. A loose bar is not a precision claim; it is wide enough that only a real fault trips it.
_provenance.notIndependent: The mean lunar node is the same polynomial in the generator and in engine.js, so pinning it catches a typo or a sign flip and cannot catch a wrong polynomial. The true node is not pinned at all: it is an osculating element with no closed form here.
_provenance.notAvailable: A JPL DE kernel would beat plan94 for Jupiter and Saturn. naif.jpl.nasa.gov is not reachable from the build environment, so de440s was not used. Switching EPHEMERIS to 'de440s' is the only change needed if it becomes available.
_provenance.ascendantMethod: Computed by intersecting the ecliptic with the horizon plane as vectors and selecting the rising root, not by the closed form engine.js uses, so the two are genuinely comparable.
